card: This PR fixes a bug in `removeForReorg` where valid BIP68 transactions spending unconfirmed inputs are erroneously evicted from the mempool alongside their descendants after a reorg lowers the chain tip. Transactions cached lockpoints assuming confirmation at the old tip plus one; when the tip lowers, stale cached lockpoints cause sequence-lock checks to fail even though the transaction is still valid. The change recalculates lockpoints via `CalculateLockPointsAtTip` before evicting, only dropping transactions that genuinely fail at the new tip. It fixes issue #35007 and includes functional tests covering height-based, mixed-input, and time-based relative lock scenarios.
changed_since_previous: Refactored the validation logic into a clean fast-path check and added a counterpart functional test (`test_reorg_unsatisfied_lock_evicted`) to ensure genuinely unsatisfied locks are still evicted along with their descendants.
evidence: Closes issue #35007: 'removeForReorg incorrectly evicts valid BIP68 transactions with mempool parents after invalidateblock'
The PR description provides a standalone reproducer script demonstrating false evictions on unpatched nodes

Adds functional test coverage in `test/functional/feature_bip68_sequence.py` verifying that valid BIP68 transactions (including mixed inputs and lowered median-time-past cases) stay in the mempool while genuinely unsatisfied locks are still evicted
problem: When a reorganization lowers the chain tip or median time past, transactions spending unconfirmed parents have lockpoints cached against the old tip plus one. Because `TestLockPointValidity` can still return true (for instance, when unconfirmed inputs default to genesis height or when confirmed inputs survive the reorg), `removeForReorg` evaluates sequence locks against stale lockpoint values and incorrectly evicts valid BIP68 transactions and all their descendants from the mempool.

risk.why: A flaw in reorg lockpoint recalculation could retain invalid transactions in the mempool after a reorg or cause block template generation failures.

summary: Recalculates BIP68 lockpoints during mempool reorg processing whenever cached lockpoints fail either the validity test or the sequence-lock check at the new chain tip. Previously, transactions with cached lockpoints that passed validity were evicted immediately if sequence locks failed against the lower tip. With this change, `MaybeUpdateMempoolForReorg` recalculates lockpoints at the new tip and only evicts the transaction and its descendants if the freshly recalculated sequence locks fail.
